title: Claude API Basics
description: Learn how the Claude API works, make your first API request, and understand the fundamentals of integrating Claude into applications.

data.text: The Claude API lets developers send requests to Claude programmatically and receive responses. Instead of chatting with Claude through a web interface, your application sends an HTTP request with a prompt, and Claude returns a response. This is how companies build AI-powered features into their products — from chatbots to content generation tools to analysis pipelines.

The Claude API follows a simple request-response pattern. Your application sends a POST request to the Anthropic API endpoint with your API key, the model you want to use, and your prompt. Claude processes the request and returns a structured response containing the generated text. The entire interaction happens over HTTPS.

data.text: To make your first API request, you need an Anthropic API key (available from console.anthropic.com), a way to send HTTP requests (curl, Postman, or any programming language), and a basic understanding of JSON. The simplest request uses the messages endpoint with a single user message.

data.title: Security best practices for API keys:
items: Never commit API keys to version control (GitHub, GitLab, etc.)
Use environment variables or a secrets manager to store keys
Create separate keys for development and production environments
Rotate keys periodically and revoke keys that are no longer needed
Use the minimum permissions necessary for each key

data.text: Claude API pricing is based on the number of tokens processed (input + output). Input tokens are what you send to Claude (your prompt + any documents); output tokens are what Claude generates in response. Different Claude models have different pricing tiers. Claude Sonnet is the cost-effective default; Claude Opus is more expensive but more capable for complex tasks.

terms.definition: The primary API endpoint for sending conversational requests to Claude.
The maximum number of tokens Claude can generate in a single response. Set this to control response length.
A parameter that controls randomness. Lower values (0.0) produce focused, deterministic output. Higher values (1.0) produce more creative, varied output.
A special parameter that sets Claude's behavior across the conversation, similar to custom instructions in the web app.

data.text: The Claude API returns standard HTTP status codes. 200 means success, 400 means a bad request (check your JSON), 401 means invalid API key, 429 means rate limited (you have sent too many requests), and 500 means an Anthropic server error. Always implement retry logic with exponential backoff for 429 and 500 errors.

data.title: Cost awareness
data.text: API costs can add up quickly if you are not careful. Always set max_tokens to a reasonable limit, monitor your usage in the Anthropic console, and use prompt caching (covered in the next lesson) to reduce costs for repeated requests.

data.title: API basics recap
points: The Claude API uses a simple HTTP request-response pattern
Requests go to api.anthropic.com with your API key and model choice
Pricing is based on tokens — both input and output count
Use environment variables for API key storage
Always implement error handling and retry logic
